results.fact: Scramble grade of the standard finish
results.evidence: The 2003 enchainment party's feature article calls Ottohorn class 3 and one of the few Southern Picket summits that is not fifth class, and a 2011 party also found it 3rd-class scrambling until a fresh rockfall zone forced two 5.7 pitches; the same 2003 party's short report lists the east ridge as class 4. Sources therefore span class 3 to 4, so 'consistently class 3' overstates and a flat 'Class 4' understates; the row's own descent_text (Class 3 with a short Class 4 step) and pro_needs (Class 3-4) already say 3-4.

results.fact: Route identity: 'West Ridge' 2017 line vs an east-ridge description
results.evidence: The overview and hazards say this is a 2017 west-ridge first-ascent line whose grade, pitch count and length are not recorded, yet rock_grade, pitch_detail, climbing_route, pro_needs and descent_text describe the 1961 standard east ridge from the Otto-Himmel col with grades. The Southeast Route row covers that standard line. Settling it needs an owner decision on whether this row is the 2017 west ridge (and should drop the east-ridge grade/pitch detail) or a duplicate of the standard route; no source describes a 2017 west ridge in detail.

A Picket Range overview places the Barrier crossing at the lower end of the Terror Glacier and mentions moats and crevasses on the approach to the Otto-Himmel col, which argues against 'non-glaciated', but no second independent source states whether the Crescent Creek side below the col is glaciated enough to require roped glacier travel and crevasse rescue. A topo/trip report stating glacier travel on the south side of the col would settle it.
